models.observations: Three inhabited glazed spires step down around the shared podium. The garden tiers, axial street stair and gold-supported beacon crown retain a recognizable profile across all three LODs.

Twin roofed entry pylons break the oval bowl at the front. The outer arcade and field contrast with the light seating. Terracotta, shaded medieval seats and warmer Renaissance stone remain legible at 64 px.

The rear spectator canopy follows the open arena on a visible row of posts. Gates and ochre bollards give the sparse bowl a human scale. The press box and corner piers shift from steel blue to warm gold.
The glazed commentators’ box rises above brick concentric terraces. The entrance posts, pennon and bonded outer arches remain readable when the Modern row shifts the bowl toward concrete.

Crossed logs, the angular flame, small pail and folded blue cloth give the gathering place character. Dawn versus Iron had no 64 px thumbnail pixel change above 12/255 in any RGB channel. The LOD2 loses both benches entirely.
defects: Use an age-responsive material across the visible seats or hearth so the three early ages are visibly distinct at 64 px.
Preserve the two benches as simple supported seat silhouettes at LOD2.

models.observations: Pale stone curbing, carved benches and the little flag distinguish the civic hearth. The LOD2 triptych loses both wing-like seats and substitutes an isolated fire pedestal.
defects: Retain simplified versions of both stone benches at LOD2 so the gathering place preserves its outside profile.

models.observations: A clean column portico and wide civic stair sit between two lower pavilions and matching topiary. The roof shifts visibly between the three age rows and the portico remains legible at the lowest mesh.
A glazed canopy spans the civic steps between cream wings. Domed rooflight, flag and paired shrubs soften the square block. The Ascension capitals and columns pick up gold around the cyan canopy.

A clock turret extends the axial municipal hall. The planted fronts, flag and pediment keep the orderly Human character in both the red-brick and pale Modern views. All three meshes retain the clock and entrance mass.

Twin ribbed grandstands, floodlights and field lines identify a sports ground immediately. Both age rows present nearly identical ivory canopy masses and blue seats at 64 px. Most visible age change is confined to narrow posts.
defects: Use a more age-responsive canopy panel or broad fascia so the Information and Ascension versions clearly separate at phone size.

models.observations: Long burgundy shelters frame the green pitch, blue seat banks and little goal frames. The four lamp clusters and raised scoreboard are readable at full size. Both LOD reductions keep the two stands and exposed grass.
Deep gable, chimney and oak front porch contrast with the striped terrace awning, projecting tankard and amber window. The surface audit found four coincident pairs on each of LOD0 and LOD1.
defects: Separate the front foundation and adjacent trim at z=-0.49 around (-0.450145,0.107,-0.49). Check all four exposed pairs on LOD0 and LOD1.

models.observations: The rooftop dome and glazing strip update the familiar little pub. The tankard and shaded outdoor tables still identify it at 64 px. The exposed stone/trim overlap remains on LOD0 and LOD1.
defects: Separate the front foundation and trim at (-0.450145,0.107,-0.49), then recheck exposed faces across all LODs.

models.observations: The dormer over the brick taproom, tall chimney, tankard and tables make the street frontage distinct. LOD0 and LOD1 each have four exposed front foundation/trim intersections.
defects: Repair coplanar front foundation/trim faces near (-0.450145,0.107,-0.49), then check both LOD0 and LOD1.

models.observations: A high roof covers an open stage with red tied curtains and gold crest. Crescent front benches part for a central stair. Roof and bench hues distinguish the three age rows while stage and seating survive LOD2.

The faceted shell, illuminated medallion, mountain backdrop and red curtains make a lively stage. The ivory roof remains nearly unchanged in both ages. The piers end around y=0.938 below the folded shell at x=±0.667.
defects: Give the shell or visible proscenium a broad age-responsive surface for a clear phone-scale change.
Extend load-carrying stage piers to the local sloped soffit or add visible capital/rafter contact at every LOD.

models.observations: The high fly wall, marquee lamps, painted scenery and gathered curtains read as a performance venue. Brick rear and seating walls become light Modern concrete. Reduced meshes keep the stage, fly building and two curved seating banks.

The paired seats now change from honey timber through earthen brown to dark Iron planks around a lighter stone hearth. The serialised LOD2 keeps two seat blocks visibly grounded and separated from the flame.
Both flanking stone benches remain in the low silhouette. The near view preserves the vessel, layered white stone coping and little pennon. The three levels maintain the same overall width.
The two large canopies switch from panelled steel to warm gold in the 64px age pair. The green field, floodlights, two banks of blue seating and end scoreboard all remain legible.
The repaired jambs now clear the stone plinth and the serialized surface audit is clean across all three levels. Both ages keep their distinct roof, tapered chimney, striped awning and large tankard.
The exposed plinth/trim conflict is gone at all LODs. The glazed roof drum, patio awning and tankard remain intact in both the cool-metal and gilt frames.
No exposed surface pairs remain around the front footing on any level. The dormer, sign and shaded tables are still recognizable in both the brick and Modern variants.

The new shell bears on the side piers and the Information/Ascension roofs now clearly change from steel to gold. In both original-size images the dark backing wall protrudes through each flat eave: its top is y=.9585 and the eave top is y=.958.
defects: Lower only the future scenery back-wall top below the .958 eaves to eliminate the visible dark ticks at both roof edges. Preserve the existing pier/soffit contacts.

models.observations: The original-size Information and Ascension previews now show uninterrupted metal eaves above the side piers. Lowering the dark backdrop clears both eave surfaces. The 64-pixel pair and the three serialized LOD views preserve the folded roof, seating and red curtains.

rounds.critic: Independent Human building critic, repair round 1
rounds.method: Inspected all mapped age PNGs, serialized LOD0/1/2, and era siblings from two unpainted 64-pixel angles. Compared painted side and rear LOD1 views. Verified each mesh and manifest with check_entry and SHA-bound exposed-face and shell checks.

models.observations: Three staggered glazed towers step up to a supported ring and suspended-looking crystal. Their gold bands and the small door on the ivory base give the tall group a readable scale. The three levels retain the tiered skyline. Serialized triangle counts are 2338, 1332, 490 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The high curved spectator canopy rises over a ring of open seating. Its thin uprights are still visible at medium distance, and the flag, scoreboard and front gate mark the approach. The canopy separates it from the open classical bowl. Serialized triangle counts are 984, 560, 288 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The high orange flame stands above a built stone hearth, with cut stone benches on two sides. The pennant, individual logs and step in the rim make it read as a tended public fire. The reduced meshes preserve the seated layout. Serialized triangle counts are 550, 313, 173 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The pediment and columns frame a flight of civic steps between two lower wings. The slate and terracotta skins preserve that hierarchy. The central columns and approach stay clear at medium distance. Serialized triangle counts are 510, 290, 144 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

Layered flat wings, an inclined glass canopy and a small offset dome replace the tiled council roof. The wide stair still reaches a supported public portico and the paired planted pots give the entrance scale. Serialized triangle counts are 567, 322, 174 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

An asymmetric clock tower interrupts the long roof behind the portico and remains above it in both grey views. The brick base, formal stairs, planters and pennon retain the public-square frontage. Serialized triangle counts are 604, 344, 188 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The two long canopies curve along the same touchlines above the same bleachers, with unchanged stadium footprint, goals and scoreboard placement. The grey profiles remain very close despite the taller canopy curvature. Serialized triangle counts are 960, 546, 264 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.
defects: Give the future stadium a substantially different roof or seating structure that reads from both angles. Preserve the pitch, entry and structural supports.

models.observations: Two banks of roofed seating flank a marked green pitch, with goals, a scoreboard and corner lights. The entrances and roof supports remain visible at middle distance, and the field reads along its long axis. Serialized triangle counts are 924, 526, 264 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The steep gable runs into a projecting entry porch. A mug sign, striped awning and outdoor table give the timber-framed inn a clear public face. The medium model retains the sign beneath the roof. Serialized triangle counts are 742, 422, 216 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

A lower roof with a dormer replaces the cross-gabled porch and a tall flue rises behind the brick hall. The striped side shelter, barrel and mug sign preserve the inn’s identity. Serialized triangle counts are 694, 394, 184 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The round timber stage and raked crescent seating are open to the promenade. A raised lighting bridge stands on splayed legs and pennants mark the entries. Both angles retain the open stage and curved seating at middle distance. Serialized triangle counts are 638, 324, 189 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2. Its largest directed LOD0 corner match with another era is 0.0%.

The tall fly loft and low street marquee distinguish the opera house from the older open stage. At medium distance the side and rear brick walls retract into triangles, leaving daylight through the hall, and the loft cap deforms. Serialized triangle counts are 316, 180, 88 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2. Its largest directed LOD0 corner match with another era is 0.0%.
defects: Restore whole walls and solid roof and fly-loft planes in LOD1. Take the budget from marquee lights or other small detail. Compare at 215, 145 and 35 degrees.

rounds.critic: Independent Human building critic, repair round 2
rounds.method: Reviewed current rendered age PNGs, both unpainted 64-pixel family views, all three serialized LODs and painted 190-pixel LOD1 views at 215, 145 and 35 degrees. Verified check_entry, the 60% LOD1 ceiling and the current GLB-bound surface and shell survey.

models.observations: The mid-distance towers retain their individual glass drums and gold bands. The support beneath the high ring reads against the open sky from both sides, and the stair still meets the base door. Serialized triangle counts are 2338, 1332, 490 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The opening in the stone seating ring is visible from the front and reverse angles. At medium distance the pennant, firewood and alternating rim blocks still frame the single flame. Serialized triangle counts are 550, 313, 173 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The center portico preserves daylight between its columns at medium distance. Both side wings keep their smaller roofs and the rear wall closes beneath the long hall roof. Serialized triangle counts are 510, 290, 144 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The cantilevered glass entry canopy and flat side roofs read separately in all three mid-distance angles. The central entry, columns and stepped approach remain open below the canopy. Serialized triangle counts are 567, 322, 174 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The clock lantern projects above the long brick roof at LOD1, including on the reverse view. Two side pavilions, columns and planted entrance steps preserve the forum layout. Serialized triangle counts are 604, 344, 188 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

A continuous elevated ring spans a rounded bowl with raked tiers, an open entrance and a green playing field. Uprights support the ring in the medium views. Both grey angles distinguish this structure from the industrial twin canopies. Serialized triangle counts are 1176, 688, 308 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The paired touchline canopies remain supported above stepped blue bleachers at middle distance. The goals and scoreboards locate the ends of the long field, clearly distinct from the future ring stadium. Serialized triangle counts are 924, 526, 264 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The projecting gabled doorway, hanging mug and striped side canopy remain identifiable at LOD1. The covered table is still readable on the near side and the long rear wall stays closed under the pitched roof. Serialized triangle counts are 742, 422, 216 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The dormer and tall narrow flue remain visible across the middle roof. A flush entrance, mug sign and side awning keep the brick hall recognizable after the barrel detail drops away. Serialized triangle counts are 694, 394, 184 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

The formerly torn brick auditorium is closed on both sides and across the back at LOD1. The fly-loft cap and pitched roof remain continuous above the lit street marquee. The profile is distinct from both era siblings in grey. Serialized triangle counts are 316, 156, 88 at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.

rounds.critic: RC4 independent Human and Dwarf art critic, three-view serialized LOD review

models.observations: Two facing roofed grandstands leave an open rectangular contest floor. The small end gates and blue railings give the approach a human scale. Both banks retain their seating and supports at distance, distinct from the round arenas and the single-ended theater stage.

The clock tower stands independently beside a tiered polygonal assembly hall. The low public entry reads against the round room, and the illuminated windows add scale at close range. The tower and round chamber stay separate in both far views.

The broad top-lit drum rises over a narrower blue glazed room. A serving entrance and freestanding tables make the public use apparent from the front. At distance the outer seating and narrower stem still separate it from the earlier gabled taproom.

A conical brewery tower sits beside a brick taproom, with large horizontal casks at the junction. The casks mark the approach and the Human gable anchors the composition. The second roof and tower remain separate in both far views.
